title: California security deposit limit (Civ. Code § 1950.5)
requirement: A landlord may not demand or receive security exceeding one month's rent, in addition to the first month's rent paid at occupancy, and must account for and return the remainder within 21 days after the tenant vacates. Small landlords (natural persons or family LLCs owning no more than two rental properties and four units) may charge up to two months' rent, unless the tenant is a service member.
key_value: 1 month's rent; 2 months' rent for small landlords
coverage_conditions: Security for a rental agreement for residential property used as the tenant's dwelling.

applicability.per_tenancy: Does not apply to security collected or demanded before July 1, 2024.

exemptions: Security collected or demanded before July 1, 2024; advance payment of six months' rent where the lease term is six months or longer; higher security for service members subject to written statement and return rules.
penalty: A landlord who in bad faith fails to comply with the itemized-statement requirements is not entitled to claim any amount of the security.
quoted_span: (c) (1) Except as provided in paragraph (2), (3), or (5), a landlord shall not demand or receive security, however denominated, in an amount or value in excess of an amount equal to one month's rent, in addition to any rent for the first month paid on or before initial occupancy.
